task: Write one sentence of your own using the word chastise. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know chastise should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The league formally chastised the club for fielding an ineligible player, and the statement stayed pinned to its website all season.
To correct someone is neutral repair, far milder than chastise's severe rebuke.
Excoriate goes further than chastise — criticism so savage it strips the skin off in public.

To castigate is to reprimand severely, often before an audience — chastise's near-twin, and the two overlap heavily. The shade of difference: castigate leans toward the public lashing, delivered for onlookers, while chastise leans official — the severe rebuke from authority that lands on the record and stays there.

To discipline is to correct with penalties, and it can be entirely neutral and procedural — a matter of policy, with no anger in it. Chastise is the rebuke itself: severe words from authority, condemnation put on the record. You can be disciplined without a single harsh word; to chastise is to say the harsh words.
